title: Advisory file soft-locks (collision-avoidance — NOT the exactly-once handoff claim)

epic.name: Coordination Bus v2 (re-scoped): Repo Coordination Bus

scope_clarification: PANEL CLARIFICATION (do not conflate with 40.B1): this story is ADVISORY, NON-EXCLUSIVE COLLISION-AVOIDANCE on FILE targets — two sessions CAN hold a soft-lock on the same file (AC-40.4.4), it only informs, it never blocks. That is the OPPOSITE of what a handoff needs. The exactly-once, first-writer-wins, 409-already_claimed HANDOFF CLAIM is 40.B1 (the channel_claims table, UNIQUE(tenant,project,ref)). The panel flagged that v1 let US-40.4's file soft-lock masquerade as covering handoff claims — it does not. Keep the two distinct: 40.4 = 'don't both edit foo.ex'; 40.B1 = 'exactly one agent picks up handoff #812'. This story is retained (collision-avoidance is real value) but is NOT on the critical A-E claim/discovery path and must never be cited as the handoff-claim primitive.

story.as_a: coding agent about to edit a specific file
story.i_want_to: post an advisory claim on that file (with a short TTL) that other sessions can see
story.so_that: two sessions on different machines don't unknowingly edit the same file and collide

rationale: The collision-avoidance primitive deferred from v1. It is built ENTIRELY on the existing channel post model (refs.file + a short expiry) — no new table — and stays advisory: it informs, it never blocks. The whole point is cooperative awareness among a single tenant's agents, so a claim is a signal, and a dead session's claim must self-expire so it can't wedge a file forever.

background.reference: docs/repo-coordination-bus.md §3.2, §3.6; built on channel_posts (refs) + a per-key upsert
background.includes: A claim is a channel post with key = "claim:<file>", refs.file set, and a SHORT expires_at override (minutes, not 30 days); release deletes it (US-39.7) or lets it expire.

acceptance_criteria.description: claim(project_id, target) posts a channel entry with key "claim:<target>", refs.file=target, and a short TTL via an optional ttl_seconds arg on the write path SERVER-CLAMPED to [min, max] minutes (e.g. 1..60) — this is the ONE place expires_at is caller-influenced (v1 fixes it at now+30d), so the clamp bounds are a stated invariant. Upserts on the hardened 5-column slot key (tenant, project, agent_id, session, key — the server-stamped agent_id was added to channel_posts_session_key_uidx at migration 20260718000000:22-25, so the slot key is NOT the old 4-column (tenant, project, session, key)) so a session refreshes its own claim. NEVER blocks the caller (advisory).

channel_recent / the TEAM CHANNEL block surface active claims distinctly ('claimed: <file> by <agent/host>, <age>'), so a session sees a live claim before editing — but the system does NOT prevent the edit (advisory only).

release(project_id, target) removes the caller's claim. Since US-39.7 deletes by post id only (not by key), this needs a delete-by-(tenant, project, agent_id, session, key) path (the same hardened 5-column slot key as AC-40.4.1) OR an upsert-to-already-expired (expires_at in the past) — specify which; v1 ships neither, so add the minimal one. A claim also self-expires via its short TTL + the sweep, so a crashed/dead session can never hold a file indefinitely.
Claims are per-session (a session claims for itself); two sessions can hold claims on the same file (advisory — the UI/agent decides). claim/release are exposed as MCP tools.

test_cases.name: claim appears as an active claim
expected_results: an active claim on lib/foo.ex is listed

test_cases.name: claim self-expires (dead session can't wedge)
preconditions: a claim with a past expires_at
steps: run the sweep / read live claims
expected_results: the expired claim is gone / not surfaced

test_cases.name: claim never blocks a concurrent editor
preconditions: session A holds a claim on foo.ex
expected_results: B's claim succeeds (advisory); both visible; no error/lock rejection

technical_notes: Reuse channel_post with a claim key convention + a short per-post expires_at override — add an optional ttl_seconds arg to the write path (server clamps it) rather than a new table.

Surface claims in the consumer (US-39.6 SessionStart injection — the retained consumer surface; the running-session turn-boundary pull formerly numbered US-40.3 moved to the claude-config companion, so target US-39.6 / the companion, NOT the removed US-40.3): prefer the INDEXED `kind = 'claim'` filter introduced by US-40.A4 over an unindexed `key LIKE 'claim:%'` prefix scan — A4's `kind` (panel agreed-gap #7) exists precisely to replace O(n) key-prefix scans at fleet volume. If 40.A4's `kind` has not landed, the `key LIKE 'claim:%'` scan is the fallback, but the indexed kind is the target once available.
MCP: claim/release tools; both agent key.
Explicitly advisory: no server-side edit prevention — this is coordination, not a mutex.
